archetype: suburban split-level detached house with offset living and sleeping floors, attached garage and sloped residential lot
ground_program: street-facing front walk rising from the sidewalk or roadside verge to a sheltered main entrance at the intermediate landing level
entry foyer forming the central split point between the upper living/sleeping level and lower utility/recreation level
attached single-car garage with a full vehicle approach, internal mudroom door and rear service access
lower recreation room with exterior-grade windows, storage and direct relation to the rear yard
laundry and mechanical room grouped near the garage and lower stair without occupying a circulation route
lower half-bath or utility washroom accessible from the recreation and service spaces
rear patio or stoop connected to the lower level and feathered into the sloped yard
foundation, retaining and drainage elements responding to the split-level grade rather than flattening the lot into a generic slab
upper_program: upper living room oriented toward the street with a coherent furniture zone clear of stair landings
kitchen and dining area sharing a functional service relationship and direct rear-facing light or yard outlook
short hall connecting three compact bedrooms and a full bathroom without routing through private rooms
primary bedroom with a distinct storage wall or closet zone
secondary bedrooms sized and furnished as actual sleeping rooms rather than empty boxes
roof volume following the offset floor massing with a legible ridge and attached-garage roof relationship
circulation: the main entrance lands at a real intermediate floor from which one supported stair flight rises to living spaces and one descends to lower service/recreation spaces
both stair flights have continuous headroom, supported landings and guard conditions where exposed
garage occupants can reach the mudroom, foyer and house interior without crossing through the vehicle bay
upper bedrooms and bathroom connect through a common hall independent of the living-room furniture zone
rear-yard access remains available from the lower level even when the front approach is damaged
damage_constraints: preserve the defining split-level section, central intermediate landing and at least one usable stair connection between each surviving occupied level
concentrate primary failure on one rear or side corner so the house remains recognizable rather than reducing it by rectangular deletion
allow partial roof collapse to follow rafters, ridge and supporting wall failure with rubble accumulating below the failed span
keep the attached garage legible with its vehicle opening, slab and interior service relationship even if its outer corner is damaged
damage windows, doors, railings and roof fragments together with their supporting geometry so no floating attachments remain
retain enough kitchen, bedroom, bathroom and utility evidence for the domestic program to remain inferable
preserve terrain contact, retaining conditions and drainage cues around surviving foundation edges
derive damaged and occupied variants only from this immutable clean master

required_manual_checks: the structure reads immediately as a split-level suburban house rather than a stacked rectangular two-storey box
the entrance landing, upper flight and lower flight connect actual walkable floors with supported stairs and sufficient headroom
garage, mudroom, laundry/mechanical and rear-yard service circulation are coherent and player-scale usable
living, kitchen/dining, bedrooms and bathroom form a plausible domestic layout with meaningful furnishing zones
the offset floor masses and roof geometry visibly express the split-level section from exterior views
foundation and yard grading meet the structure without floating walls, buried doors or unsupported slabs
damage follows structural gravity while preserving the defining split-level circulation and domestic identity
